items.title: Tom Lellis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 31, 2007
items.q: We did it live. Yeah. And John Clayton conducted.

ctx.x: Yeah. That must have been a heck of a feeling when you did that with the Metropole Orchestra. Did you do that live?

We did it live. Yeah. And John Clayton conducted. So it was the thrill of my life. It came out of the blue. Mark Murphy had told me to send my material to the Netherlands. And then I did, I sent the material and I got an email maybe eight months, nine months later, maybe a year. And the producer said that he just kept listening to my record. He just kept

playing it and he goes back to it. And he said, “I can’t promise you anything but I’m keeping you in mind.” And then I did a performance at the IAJE in New York in 1998 with Joe Locke and Tony Marino, who was just on the gig last night, and Jamey Haddad. And he was there and we signed a contract to do it the next day, for a year and a month later. I had to wait 13 months to do it, and it was the longest period. That was such a thrill. I had to keep my welled up tears down in the middle of a couple of those takes…
